one_line_summary: A local link-preview proxy that renders a safe, time-bounded snapshot of a URL so emails can show previews without sending a live browser to the original site on every click.
problem: Link previews in email and chat can expose your IP, cookies, and referral context to the linked site the moment a preview is generated, and previews can embed anything the remote server returns.
audience: Non-developer: people who want to see where a link goes before they click, or who share links and want previews without leaking a live request to the destination on every preview.
solution: A local proxy that fetches the target URL in an isolated renderer, takes a snapshot, and serves a time-bounded preview card. It applies a simple policy: no cookies forwarded, no credentials, no scripting of the local context, and a clear indication that the preview is a snapshot, not a live visit.
key_features: Local preview endpoint that fetches a URL and returns a safe snapshot card
No credential or cookie forwarding to the target
Time-bounded preview with expiry so the snapshot is not treated as fresh forever
Policy report per preview: what was fetched, when, and what was redacted
Configurable allow/deny list for preview targets
mvp_scope: HTTP server with a /preview endpoint, a fetch-and-snapshot routine that strips credentials, a simple policy engine for allow/deny, expiry metadata, and a JSON policy report alongside the snapshot.
tests_plan: Unit tests for policy allow/deny and expiry handling
Unit tests for credential stripping in the request builder
Integration test against a local static test server that confirms no cookies/credentials are sent and the preview card carries expiry + policy metadata
